title: Throwing a stoneware salt pig
subtitle: A deep, open-top stoneware jar for keeping salt at the hob, with a wide low opening
excerpt: A salt pig is a wide, slightly flared open jar used for storing cooking salt at the hob , the wide low mouth makes it easy to pinch salt without a lid. This thrown version is 100 mm tall, 90 mm in diameter at the widest point, and uses grogged stoneware for extra thermal stability. Fired to cone 6.
sourceNotes: Stoneware salt pig throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage at which the form holds its shape for trimming and foot-ring work
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)
Pyrometric measure of heat-work in a kiln. Cone 6 approx 1220 degrees C
Pre-fired ground clay added to a clay body for strength, texture, and thermal resistance

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.
A salt pig's shape is a squat, belly-outward jar , widest about two-thirds of the way up, then drawing in slightly toward the rim. The wide low opening makes it easy to reach salt without a lid.
Grogged
stoneware handles kitchen thermal cycles well. The inside is fully glazed; the outside is glazed to the foot-ring, leaving the base clay bare.
Centre, open, and throw
Wedge 500 g of grogged stoneware. Centre on the wheel head.
Open a 55 mm floor, leaving 10 mm at the base. Pull walls to 100 mm height with an initial straight cylinder.

Shape the belly by pressing outward with the inside hand fingers at a point two-thirds up from the base, while the outside hand supports the wall at the same height. Make the belly bulge gradually , two or three gentle passes. The maximum width should reach about 90 mm. Keep the upper wall above the belly moving slightly inward to create the salt pig silhouette.
The rim should end up wider than the body base but not as wide as the belly , the classic salt pig mouth is a wide open funnel. Compress and smooth the rim with the chamois leather.
Wire off the wheel. Allow to dry to
leather-hard
Trim the foot-ring

Centre upside-down on the wheel head at leather-hard. Trim a foot-ring 5 mm tall using the loop tool. The base will be heavier than on a thin-walled piece so more material needs to come out from inside the foot-ring.
Bisque and glaze
Allow to reach bone-dry.
Bisque
fire to
cone
06 (approx 1000 degrees C).
Glaze the inside fully. Glaze the outside by dipping or brushing to just above the foot-ring. Clean glaze from the foot-ring and base. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.cause: The wall at the belly point was too thin to hold the outward pressure
rows.fix: Build the belly more gradually over two passes. The wall should be at least 7 mm thick at the widest belly point before you push outward.

rows.problem: Rim too narrow , looks like a vase not a salt pig
rows.cause: The inside hand did not flare the rim enough at the final stage
rows.fix: At the rim stage, use the index finger inside the top rim to gently press it outward while the wheel turns slowly.
